To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
5-O- feruloyl-β-D- xylopyranosyl-(1→3)-α-L-arabinopyranose is a novel feruloylated monoarabinoside identified in maize, wheat, and wheat bran.
(i) 5-O- feruloyl- α-L- arabinoside is the major form of F- AXOS in maize and (ii) the content of F-AXOs in maize is higher than in wheat.
the content of 5-O- feruloyl- α-L-arabinofurano- side chains in maize and wheat are higher than previously reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and identification of F-AXOs from maize, wheat and wheat bran.
the isolation and characterization of F-AXO mono- and oligomers from undigested maize and wheat as well as from samples subjected to simulated gastric fluid with and without enzymes.
the isolation and identification of F-AXOs from maize and wheat, and provides a basis for future research on the prebiotic properties of maize and wheat F-AXOS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the F-AXOS content of maize is higher than wheat and that the F- AXOS released during digestion of maize and wheat is higher than that released from wheat bran or aleurone.
F-AXOS are present in maize and wheat and are resistant to digestion under pH and gastric conditions.

maize has higher levels of feruloyl arabinoxylans than wheat and that the level of these feruloyl-arabinosides in maize and wheat is positively correlated to the level of bound ferulic acid in the grain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maize and wheat are good sources of F-AXO, and their content can increase during simulated gastrointestinal digestion.
F-AXOS is present at higher concentrations in maize compared to wheat, and the level of F- AXOS produced during simulated digestion is positively correlated to the bound FA content of a given sample.
F-AXOS are released during simulated gastric digestion and are likely to be present in the large intestine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
F-AXOS are present in maize and wheat and are resistant to digestion under simulated gastric conditions.
F-AXOS are resistant to digestion under gastric conditions and can be isolated from undigested or digested samples.
F-AXOS are released during in vitro gastrointestinal digestion of wheat and maize and can be used as a source of prebiotics and antioxidants.
